title: CFO AI Governance Framework
summary: A finance-led framework for evaluating AI investment, controls, ownership, evidence, and reporting.

sections.heading: Start with the decision, not the model
sections.content: Define the business decision, accountable executive, affected workflow, financial exposure, and evidence required before evaluating a model or vendor.

sections.heading: Create an AI investment register
sections.content: Maintain one finance-visible register of material AI initiatives. Record cost, owner, data used, deployment status, controls, expected benefit, and review date.

sections.heading: Separate approval from assurance
sections.content: The executive sponsoring an AI initiative should not be the only person assessing its evidence. Finance, security, legal, risk, and the operating owner should have explicit review responsibilities.

sections.heading: Report outcomes and exceptions
sections.content: Board reporting should distinguish pilots, deployed systems, measured outcomes, control exceptions, and unresolved risks. Demonstrations and projected value are not realized value.

title: CFO ERP Implementation Evidence Checklist
summary: A control-focused checklist for evaluating ERP scope, cost, readiness, security, migration, and benefits.

sections.heading: Approve a bounded scope
sections.content: The business case should identify the legal entities, processes, reports, integrations, controls, and data included in the implementation. Unbounded transformation language is not a testable scope.

sections.heading: Build a complete cost estimate
sections.content: Include software, implementation partners, internal labor, migration, integration, testing, training, security, parallel operations, contingency, and post-launch support.

sections.heading: Treat data migration as financial control work
sections.content: Define source-to-target ownership, reconciliation thresholds, exception handling, retention requirements, and sign-off before migration begins.

sections.heading: Set evidence-based go-live gates
sections.content: Go-live should depend on completed controls, reconciled data, tested integrations, operational support, security review, and a documented rollback decision, not the calendar alone.

title: CFO Revenue Recognition Decision Record
summary: A structured record for documenting revenue-recognition judgments, evidence, approvals, and changes under the applicable accounting guidance.

sections.heading: Identify the contract and evidence
sections.content: Record the executed agreement, amendments, enforceable rights, payment terms, collection considerations, and the accounting period covered by the analysis.

sections.heading: Document performance obligations
sections.content: Identify the promised goods and services, the reasoning for whether they are distinct, and the evidence supporting any combination or separation judgment.

sections.heading: Record price and allocation judgments
sections.content: Document fixed and variable consideration, constraints, significant financing considerations, noncash consideration, standalone selling prices, and the allocation method.

sections.heading: Define recognition and change controls
sections.content: State whether each obligation is satisfied over time or at a point in time, the selected progress measure, source data, approval owner, reassessment triggers, and disclosure implications.
